cards.example: The discovery of penicillin was a major breakthrough that has saved millions of lives.
The groundbreaking discovery of the structure of DNA changed medicine and biology forever.
Technological innovation creates new jobs, but it can also make many traditional jobs disappear.
Machine learning allows computers to recognise faces and translate texts without being programmed step by step.
Smart speakers raise serious privacy concerns because they may record our private conversations.
Strict data protection laws in the EU limit how companies can use our personal information.
Many messaging apps use encryption so that nobody else can read your private conversations.
Scientists are looking for better ways to harness the power of the sun and the wind.

cards.example: It is worrying that so many teenagers seem to be dependent on their phones for entertainment.
The new hospital uses cutting-edge technology to diagnose cancer at a very early stage.
My grandfather loves buying the latest gadgets, but he never reads the instructions.
Wearable technology like smartwatches can track your heart rate and remind you to move more.
Social media companies are under pressure to remove hate speech from their platforms more quickly.
Never share your bank details online, because criminals can use them for identity theft.
A teenager managed to hack into the school's computer system and change his grades.
During the pandemic, misinformation about vaccines spread quickly on social media.
Social media algorithms show us content we already agree with, which can make us less open-minded.
Digital literacy is essential today, so schools should teach students how to check online sources.
Automation is likely to replace many factory jobs, so workers will need to learn new skills.
Some experts believe that robots will replace teachers one day, but I think personal contact in the classroom is irreplaceable.
Genetic engineering could help cure inherited diseases, but many people have doubts about its safety.
Cloning animals raises serious ethical questions that scientists simply cannot ignore.
Space exploration is extremely expensive, and some people think the money should be spent on Earth instead.
Scientists at the University of Szeged carry out research into new treatments for cancer.
In chemistry lessons we sometimes conduct an experiment to see how different substances react.
There is no scientific evidence that mobile phones cause cancer, but some people still worry.
Our school's computers are so outdated that they take ten minutes to start up.
The new app has such an intuitive design that even my grandmother learned to use it in minutes.
Nobody can predict which videos will go viral and which ones will be completely ignored.
Virtual reality headsets could make history lessons more exciting by taking students back in time.
Thanks to medical advances, people today live much longer than they did a century ago.
Scientists managed to develop vaccines against the coronavirus in record time.
Young people are usually more tech-savvy than their parents, so they often help them with their phones.
I tried a digital detox for a week and was surprised how much free time I suddenly had.
Engineers are trying to come up with cheaper and longer-lasting batteries for electric cars.
TikTok has become one of the most popular social media platforms among teenagers worldwide.
Some people feel that constant camera surveillance in public places threatens their freedom.
For most people, the benefits of smartphones clearly outweigh their disadvantages.
Technology is a double-edged sword: it connects people, but it can also isolate them.
Online shopping is quick and convenient; on the downside, it makes us vulnerable to online fraud.
